subject: Embeddings integration post-call: migration, dims & batching
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap — embeddings migration, dims & next steps

Thanks for the call today — great context on Everwell's search & recommendations use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned:

Summary of needs
- Migrate ~12M existing vectors from your current provider (VecStore).
- Use reranker for top-K reordering and structured output/tool-calling for attribute extraction.
- Low P99 latency target for semantic search (<60ms) and batch upserts during migration window.

Key integration notes
- SDK & auth: Redwood SDK supports API key auth (per-environment keys). We can also support scoped keys for ingestion vs. query. We'll share sample auth patterns in the SE call.
- Vector dims: Redwood supports common dims (768, 1024, 1536). Optimal choice depends on model family — for the open LLM you demo'd we recommend 1536 for best recall; 768/1024 are supported if you prefer smaller index size.
- Normalization: We support both raw vectors and normalized vectors. If you currently pre-normalize (L2), that's fine — we can accept pre-normalized data or run normalization server-side and store normalized vectors.
- Batching: For migration we recommend bulk upserts in chunks of 10k-100k depending on instance size; for runtime we suggest batch sizes of 32–256 for embeddings generation depending on latency/throughput trade-offs.
- Reranker: We can plug a reranker stage post-retrieval; we also support hybrid rescoring with signal weighting.
- Structured output/tool-calling: We can return JSON Schema-constrained outputs from LLM calls and wire them to your downstream pipeline.

Attachments & links
- Attached: redwood-embeddings-migration-checklist.pdf (migration checklist)
- Shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C4D5E6F7G8H

Next steps
1) SE deep-dive: Dev suggested Mon/Tue next week — 60m to review sample dataset + migration plan.
2) You to share a 1–2k record POC dataset (sanitized) and a sample query set.
3) We'll provide a cost estimate and migration runbook after the SE session.

If that all looks right, I'll send a calendar invite for the SE call with a proposed agenda.

—Marissa

Hi Liam — quick technical answers and migration guidance from our SE team:

1) Vector dimension strategy
- If your current vectors are 1024-d, you have two options:
  a) Re-embed all documents with the 1536-d model for improved recall (recommended for high signal domains).
  b) Keep 1024-d vectors and use a 1024-d embedding model + tuned reranker. We'll surface model-level perf tradeoffs in the SE call.

2) Normalization
- Redwood accepts either. If you pre-normalize (L2) we will store as-is and use inner-product/cosine accordingly.
- We also provide server-side normalization at ingest time (configurable) if you prefer a single normalization standard during migration.

3) Batching and memory
- For bulk upserts we recommend chunk sizes between 10k–50k vectors per request when running from a single high-memory node; monitor heap RSS and back off to 5k if you see GC spikes.
- For generation-time batching: 32–128 depending on model latency targets. Our SDK has built-in adaptive batching you can enable.

4) Migration tooling & id mapping
- We support a bulk import API + streaming upserts. Recommended flow:
  1. Export IDs + metadata from VecStore in batches.
  2. Upsert into Redwood with your original IDs to preserve references.
  3. Run a small verification job comparing top-K for a sample query set.
- We'll share a sample bulk_migrate.py script and a Migration runbook in the SE session.

5) Cost roughness
- Rough estimate: storage per vector scales linearly with dim; at 12M vectors expect ~X–Y/month (we'll provide exact numbers tied to model selection in the quote). I'll have pricing attached in the follow-up.

Proposed times for SE deep-dive: Mon Jun 29 10:00–11:00 PT or Tue Jun 30 14:00–15:00 PT. Which works for you?
